newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan game maker sees huge jump in profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan game maker sees huge jump in profits.

text.p: Japanese game software maker Capcom Co Ltd expects profits to leap by more than 30 percent a year and to set record parent current profits within five years, president Kenzo Tsujimoto said.
"I expect our parent current profit will grow more than 30 percent each year from this year, surpassing our record parent current profit in five years," Tsujimoto told Reuters in an interview.
Capcom achieved its record current profit of 14.44 billion yen ($132 million) in the year to March 31, 1994.

In the last 1995/96 business year, Capcom posted only a 3.18 billion yen ($29.1 million) parent current profit. It slumped to 2.1 billion yen ($19.2 million) in 1994/95. The firm expects that to rise to five billion yen ($45.8 million) this year.

The ambitious forecast for the years ahead is based on restructuring efforts, including a cut in the number of employees. Capcom has also focused more on improving profitability than on increasing sales, he said.
Tsujimoto also said Capcom may soon start making profits in its overseas business.
"In addition to Asian countries, we are getting a huge amount of orders for game-arcade products from the Middle East, South America and Africa," he said.

Tsujimoto predicts the game industry will continue to expand, and that in Japan alone over the next two years, the computer game software market should mushroom to over 1 trillion yen ($9.1 billion) from the present 600 billion yen ($5.50 billion), Tsujimoto said.
"To meet the situation, we needed to create a new marketing system," he said. "So, we have decided to tie-up with five other software firms in selling our products at convenience stores."
Earlier this month, six firms, including Capcom, Square Co Ltd and Namco Ltd, said they had agreed on a joint venture to market videogame software in convenience stores.
Tsujimoto expects that over the long term there will eventually be about 20 million computer game machines in Japan, up from the current six million.
If that happens Capcom's parent current profit could reach 50 billion yen ($458 million), he added.
Tsujimoto said the first game machines using the digital video disc (DVD) system should appear in 1998, and that within several years of that the system will be the mainstream in the industry.
DVD is a new recording system which has a large storage capacity and is expected to eventually make videocassette recorders and compact disc players obsolete.
Tsujimoto said he would like to keep his promise to Capcom shareholders that the company would pay a total of 97.50 yen ($0.89) in dividends in the three years ending next March.
When Capcom issued 12 billion yen ($110 million) worth of Euroyen bonds in 1994, it promised to pay average annual dividends of 32.50 yen over the following three years, he said.
But the dividend was just 15 yen in 1994/95 and 30 yen in 1995/96.
"We realise we have 52.50 yen ($0.48) to pay this year to keep the promise," Tsujimoto said. "It's a promise. We have to keep it."
At the moment, Capcom's dividend forecast for this year is just 20 yen ($0.18). ($1=109 yen)
